title: Dispatched
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/dispatches/<dispatch_id>/dispatched, application/json: the starter started the job for the dispatch. The dispatch's lease gives way to its start window, within which the starter asks for the handover, handover.schema.json. A dispatch_id that is unknown, or that is of a node pool the key does not serve, is refused 403 forbidden, with the same signed body as an unknown pool, so nobody learns whether an id exists; the control plane decides this before any 409 or 410. The signature with the pool's access key and that check authorise the request, not the id. It is refused after the lease lapsed and the dispatch went back to the queue with the same run, 409 lease_expired, and the starter then stops the job it started for that dispatch; after the dispatch ended because its work item was closed or undone, 410 gone. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. It is signed with the pool's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the starter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

external.description: The job at the provider that runs it, when the starter knows it. Absent otherwise.

type.description: The starter's word for what the job is at the provider, stored as data.

ref.description: The job's ref at the provider.

url.description: The job's page at the provider.
